answer: Agents anchor their identity by executing 10,000,000 sequential hashing iterations, a strict temporal gate requiring consistent CPU focus. A verifier challenges agents to provide a valid cipher that validates this chain, ensuring non-replayable output at the start of each epoch. An honest participant pays this cost once to establish a sturdy timber foundation, while 1,000 fakes must incur 10,000,000,000 units to mimic uniqueness before the dawn of the next window. We assume sequential cycles cannot be amortized or parallelized across multiple nodes.
